content.name: agents-cli deploy readiness (signed human approval)
content.summary: Resolve the effective agents-cli deployment plan, block for an explicit human decision, and refuse to deploy unless signed approval evidence verifies against that plan.
content.description: AISP companion to google-agents-cli-deploy. Closes the prose-only 'Never run agents-cli deploy without explicit human approval' gap (google/agents-cli#48) by composing: a real-plan resolver over cmd_deploy.py flags + agents-cli-manifest.yaml, SoulBot's existing sys.io.confirm Runtime, and the v2 BIP-340 approval verifier. Prototype resolver — several LOAD_BEARING_FIELDS have no first-class agents-cli source today and stay absent.

params.cli_flags: object, parsed agents-cli deploy flags (click dest names or --flag spellings)
params.manifest: object, loaded agents-cli-manifest.yaml, or empty for a flags-only deploy
params.approval_payload: object, optional pre-built approval envelope (normally produced by the human via sys.io.confirm)

content.system_prompt: ASSERT: AISOP skill. Strictly execute aisop.main. Align Axiom 0: Human Sovereignty and Wellbeing. The LLM identifies approve / reject / modify and routes; it never adjudicates signatures, digests, or expiry. Pass the raw approval payload to the verifier. Never synthesize, infer, complete, or auto-approve the human decision.

content.instruction: STRICTLY OBEY aisp_contract; its non_negotiable rules are inviolable; then RUN aisop.main

when_to_use: deploy an ADK agent with agents-cli and a forced human decision is required
produce or verify a plan-bound signed approval for agents-cli deploy
gate agents-cli deploy behind sys.io.confirm + deterministic evidence

non_negotiable.rule: Do not deploy without an explicit human decision on the resolved deployment plan.
When the human decision is approve, deployment must not proceed unless the attached approval evidence validates against the current effective deployment plan.
non_negotiable.enforced_by: verified{Evidence valid?}:no->blocked, and redundantly by deploy.step1:sys.assert immediately before the irreversible action

resources.when: documenting LOAD_BEARING_FIELDS and honest coverage gaps
cross-language recomputation of the v2 fixtures

aisop.main:
graph TD
    resolve_plan[Resolve effective deployment plan]
        --> human_approval[Wait for human decision]

    human_approval --> decision{Human decision}

    decision -->|approve| verify_approval[Verify approval evidence]
    decision -->|modify| modify_plan[Apply requested changes]
    decision -->|reject| cancelled[Stop without deployment]

    modify_plan --> resolve_plan
    verify_approval --> verified{Evidence valid?}

    verified -->|yes| deploy[Run agents-cli deploy]
    verified -->|no| blocked[Block deployment]

resolve_plan.step1: Call the deterministic plan resolver (scripts/approval_verifier.py resolve, which composes scripts/resolve_agents_cli_plan.py -- both local to this Skill Folder, no path outside it) with the parsed cmd_deploy.py-style CLI flags and the loaded agents-cli-manifest.yaml. Do not ask an LLM to invent the effective plan.
resolve_plan.step2: Present the complete effective deployment plan, including target, project, region, source or image revision, eval evidence, IAM/secrets status, rollback plan, and observability requirements. Fields the resolver could not map from real agents-cli state are absent — say so, do not fill them in.

human_approval.step1: Present the complete effective deployment plan, including target, project, region, source or image revision, eval evidence, IAM/secrets status, rollback plan, and observability requirements.
human_approval.step2: sys.io.confirm('Reply with approve {approval evidence}, reject {reason}, or modify {requested changes}', options=['approve', 'reject', 'modify']) -> human_response
human_approval.step3: Interpret the leading human decision and preserve the remaining human-authored content without inventing, completing, or silently altering approval evidence.

verify_approval.step1: When human_decision is approve, call the deterministic approval-verification tool with the current effective deployment plan and the preserved approval payload.
verify_approval.step2: Return the structured verification result (valid, plan_digest_matches, approved_scope_matches_current_plan, approved_scope_digest_matches, signature_valid, not_expired, decision_is_approve) as-is. Do not assert here -- the verified{Evidence valid?} routing node and deploy.step1's sys.assert are the sole gates on invalid evidence, so a rejection routes to blocked instead of raising mid-function.

modify_plan.step1: Apply the requested changes from the human modify payload to the CLI flags / manifest inputs. A modified plan necessarily returns to resolve_plan and then to a new human confirmation.
modify_plan.step2: Discard any previous approval envelope. Approval for the previous plan must never silently carry over.

deploy.step1: sys.assert('approval_verification.valid == true', 'The deployment approval does not authorize the current effective plan')
deploy.step2: Call scripts/approval_verifier.py deploy-check with the already-approved plan object and the current live cli_flags/manifest. Re-resolve a fresh plan from that live state and compare every execution-relevant field (deployment_target, gcp_project, region, service_name, service_account, resource_sizing, network_exposure, secret_policy_digest, source_revision). If any field diverges, refuse (fail closed). Do not treat the original flags as authoritative without this bind — a native agents-cli deploy --plan-json does not exist yet.
deploy.step3: sys.assert('deploy_check.bound == true', 'Live flags/manifest no longer resolve to the approved execution-relevant plan')
deploy.step4: Only then run agents-cli deploy with those same live flags. Do not re-resolve ad hoc in the shell after this check.

cancelled.step1: Stop without deployment. Record the human reject reason.

blocked.step1: Block deployment. Surface the structured verification checks (plan_digest_matches, approved_scope_matches_current_plan, approved_scope_digest_matches, signature_valid, not_expired, decision_is_approve) without asking the LLM whether the evidence 'looks valid'.
